description: AstraPulse07 is a solo team from Yükseliş Koleji in Antalya, Türkiye. Team member: Azra Kurt. For the challenge "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" we built Astro Sağlık – Space Station Health Mission: a 3D web game where players collect an astronaut's health data, assess the risks and act fast to keep the crew healthy. Skills: game design, web development (HTML, JavaScript, Three.js), space health research and presentation. Our team is complete.
summary: Astro Sağlık – Space Station Health Mission is a 3D web game that turns astronaut health monitoring into a hands-on mission. The player is an astronaut on a space station whose body is affected by the five hazards of human spaceflight described by NASA's Human Research Program: radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, altered gravity and a hostile closed environment. Seven live health indicators (heart, bone & muscle, immune system, radiation safety, mood, sleep and hydration) slowly drop every mission day. Each day the player runs a health scan (heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, body temperature, bone density, radiation dose, stress, sleep, hydration), assesses the data, makes a medical decision and then acts in the right module: gym, kitchen, greenhouse, comms room, sleep pod or radiation shelter. Random health alarms and solar flares test quick thinking. At the end, a Health Report Card shows the score and every indicator. The game runs offline in any browser on computers and tablets, so students can learn how astronauts stay healthy through the same loop real crews use: collect data, assess, act.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Astro Sağlık – Space Station Health Mission is a 3D health monitoring game that runs in any web browser. The player walks a blocky astronaut around a space station with Earth and the Moon in view. Seven live health indicators (Heart & vessels, Bone & muscle, Immune system, Radiation safety, Mood, Sleep & energy, Water & food) slowly drop every mission day, faster as the mission goes on. Below 25 a red alarm appears; at 0 the astronaut needs a medical evacuation and the mission ends.

HOW IT WORKS: COLLECT → ASSESS → ACT

1) Collect: at the Medical Center the player runs a daily health scan with heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, body temperature, bone density, radiation dose, stress, sleep and hydration values.

2) Assess: the player reads the numbers and chooses the riskiest area or answers a medical decision question (for example: fever 38.2 °C, tired, sore throat – what is the best action?). A wrong answer shows the right one, and every question ends with a "Real space" fact.

3) Act: the player goes to the right module – Gym (treadmill & resistance workout), Kitchen (balanced meal), Greenhouse (growing plants), Comms Room (mood check & family call), Sleep Pod or Radiation Shelter – each a short mini-game that improves one or more indicators.

Random health events (fever, heart rhythm, blurred vision, stress, bone pain, dehydration, insomnia) appear with a countdown, and a beam and arrow guide the player. On some days a solar flare hits and the player must reach the shelter in 20 seconds. At the end, a Health Report Card shows the score, stars, every indicator and a tip.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

The game teaches the same skill astronauts need on long missions: notice changes early, read the data, decide and act on your own. It is free, needs no installation and works offline on school computers and tablets. Up to 8 players can take turns on one device and compare scores on a podium, so a whole class can learn space health together.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript with the Three.js 3D library (saved locally, so no internet is needed), Web Audio API for sounds made in code, keyboard + mouse-look with a first-person camera option, and a touch joystick for tablets. Source code: https://github.com/cemyurtlak/astro-saglik

CREATIVITY AND FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Instead of a dashboard, we turned health monitoring into a game loop, so learning happens by doing. All health events are based on NASA research about the hazards of human spaceflight, exercise on the ISS, plant growth (Veggie) and space radiation. We designed it for children: simple controls, clear colors, big buttons, guidance arrows and short sessions. The game interface is currently in Turkish; an English version is our next step, together with real smartwatch data and a Mars mission mode.
